correctness.rationale: PASS. All arcs of bidirected K_{2,6} have one of the two hubs as endpoint; in/out degree at most one restricts faces to at most four arcs. Independently rebuilding the 24-arc graph, enumerating each candidate face and prohibiting cycles exactly reproduced augmented counts (1,24,192,600,600): 1417 complete faces. The deterministic ordered matching produces 624 disjoint codimension-one pairs, with SHA-256 pair digest 4b74f6d6352facf63b8331aea1dcf5cd2247daa557581d0c58e868280595c03a, and 169 unmatched four-arc faces. Independent full Hasse orientation/topological sorting checked all 4608 cover relations, with no gradient cycle. Deleting the matched empty-face/vertex pair leaves one critical zero-cell and 169 critical 3-cells; Forman theory therefore proves the INTEGRAL wedge of 169 S³, not merely its mod-two Betti rank. A separate independent enumeration of all eleven S6 conjugacy types recovered the signed fixed-face Lefschetz character (1,-1,1,1,1,-1,-5,1,1,-7,169) in the result's listed cycle order; exact Murnaghan–Nakayama character inner products recovered each of the eight nonnegative Specht multiplicities, total dimension 169. The original code additionally checks mod-2 and mod-3 boundary ranks (1,23,169,431). This is an exhaustive certificate for the finite 24-arc object, not a proof for other widths.

originality.rationale: PASS, best of knowledge. Caputi–Collari–Smith (2026) treats multipath complexes of bidirected paths and polygons, not the bidirected complete bipartite graph K_{2,6}. Caputi–Collari–Di Trani–Smith's earlier complete-bipartite calculation concerns alternating ONE-WAY orientations (and Euler data), so it cannot determine the bidirected object or S6 top homology character. The published bidirected double-star classification is for trees with adjacent hubs, not a complete bipartite digraph with many squares. Other matching/Morse complexes and a separate P6×P6 example happen to share a number 169 but have different vertices, faces and homology degrees. Targeted searches found no exact six-leaf multipath integral wedge and character result. Claims about earlier small widths are not used as decisive novelty evidence without matching primary full text; an unindexed complete-bipartite multipath classification remains residual risk.
